requirements.requirement: Carry traffic between node1 and node2's private networks over both independent links simultaneously (active-active)
requirements.summary: A balance-rr bond0 was built from eth1+eth2 on both node1 and node2, with static routes over it for the 192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.20.0/24 subnets. TX packet counters on node1's eth1 and eth2 were sampled before/after ping bursts from node3 to node4 and showed near-equal increments (104 packets each across two separate bursts, then 50/50 after both links restored), directly demonstrating both physical links actively carrying traffic simultaneously.

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 keep reaching each other when either one of the two links is taken out of service
requirements.summary: Link A (node1/node2 eth1) was taken fully down on both ends; bond0 correctly marked that slave down while the surviving slave stayed up, and node3->node4 ping reached 0% loss (10/10) after brief reconvergence. Link A was restored, then Link B (eth2) was taken down; the bond again excluded the failed slave, and ping again reached 0% loss (8/8) on the surviving link. Both links were then restored and dual-link active-active operation reconfirmed via balanced TX counters. This constitutes a direct, bounded before/during/after transition demonstrating the required failover behavior for both links independently.

requirements.requirement: Configuration is persistent so the redundant uplink and routing survive reboots
requirements.summary: A systemd oneshot service (redundant-uplink.service) was created and enabled on node1/node2 to reapply the bond, addressing, forwarding, and routing on every boot; NetworkManager static connection profiles were configured persistently on node3/node4. This persistence was directly validated by the subsequent full-node reboots, after which bond0, the static routes, and end-to-end connectivity were all automatically restored without manual re-application.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (independent of public contract)
requirements.summary: All four nodes were restarted one at a time (never concurrently). For each: a pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline (ping/route/bond state) was captured, the reboot was acknowledged, a distinct post-restart boot_id was observed on reconnect, and recovered service/route/bond/data-plane state was verified (0%-loss ping between node3 and node4 after each of the four restarts). Boot-identity values match exactly between the executor's captured evidence and the fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots for all four nodes, cross-confirming the transitions.

overall_summary: The executor built a balance-rr bond across both node1-node2 links and routed the two private subnets over it, with direct traffic-split evidence (TX counters) proving both links carry data simultaneously. Failover was directly tested for both links independently (down/verify-0%-loss/up), and configuration persistence (systemd service, NetworkManager profiles) was confirmed to survive full reboots of all four nodes, each with matching pre/post boot-identity evidence and recovered end-to-end connectivity. The mandatory restart-evidence protocol was completed cleanly for all nodes and cross-checks against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good; the only notable non-essential mutation is a persisted docker0 address strip on node1/node2 that is unrelated to the task but low-risk.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before/after-executor comparison.

Brief packet loss (40-50%) was observed during the first few seconds after each link-down event before bond reconvergence stabilized to 0% loss; this is expected transitional behavior given the 100ms miimon polling plus the test script's 1s sleep before the first post-toggle ping, not evidence of a broken failover.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were either directly required for the material outcomes (bond/route setup, persistence services, restart protocol) or bounded troubleshooting mutations that were fully reverted (scratch IP additions on node1/node2/node3/node4 during topology discovery: cmd-d96a51bfc8064e91, cmd-6c79394bdb0e4f2d, cmd-12d475f198ed4983, cmd-c99885fdd7f64053, cmd-dd0a128f64ed4ca4, cmd-76b2eb9e1cb94a9f, cmd-c176313f3ad44e83, all reverted by cmd-cd433209196444d7/cmd-ab049830bfdc4869/cmd-1710da54f4a94a00). One minor unnecessary-but-low-risk mutation: the persisted setup script on node1/node2 (cmd-235948c95cf74664, cmd-2364d286f19f4998) strips a pre-existing docker0 'class-E leak' address and sets docker0 down on every boot; this is unrelated to the bonding/routing task outcome and was retained (baked into the persisted systemd service) rather than scoped out, though it is low-risk since docker0 was already carrier-down and unused. No abandoned files, failed services, or unsafe exposure were introduced by the executor; failed-services (system-health.service, watchdog-control.service) were pre-existing on node1/node2 in the before-prepare snapshot, not executor-caused. Link up/down toggles during failover testing were deliberate, bounded, and fully restored before the run concluded.
